newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firmer, three Brent cargoes kept.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firmer, three Brent cargoes kept.

text.p: North Sea crudes posted modest gains in early Friday talk amid thin supply of benchmark Dated Brent and good demand for late August cargoes of other grades, traders said.
"The North Sea seems pretty healthy at the moment," said an oil company trader.
All three Brent cargoes due to be nominated loading dates on Friday were kept early by their equity holders and only one other Dated Brent, an Aug 13-15 loader, was available.
"Brent should stay strong for a little while because there aren't too many cargoes around," said a trader.
Prompt cash Brent intermonth spreads held firm, Aug/Sep repeating Thursday's late deal at +30 cents and Sep/Oct also trading at a steady level of -3 cents.
Brent CFDs were better bid, next week's Aug 4-8 dates pegged four cents firmer at Sep Brent +12/+16 cents. Aug 11-15 traded at Sep Brent +1 cent, also a couple of cents up on the day.
September Brent futures on the IPE slipped back, losing 24 cents to $18.71 a barrel by 1217 GMT, but brokers said the move was mainly a correction to a late spurt on Thursday.

Improving margins, given an extra leg up by news that Shell Pernis had closed its catalytic cracker earlier than expected for routine maintenance, were helping to bolster refinery interest, traders said.

There was unconfirmed talk of two, third decade August Forties cargoes trading at firmer premiums of around 40/45 cents over Dated Brent on Thursday, and Norwegian Oseberg was also looking perkier after four cargoes found homes.
Statfjord cargoes with later loading dates were also benefiting from a three-day delay in the August programme, traders said.
Sour crude in the Mediterranean was steady but interest was waning amid growing signs Iraqi exports could be flowing from the Turkish port of Ceyhan by the middle of this month.
Benchmark Russian Urals crude was still pegged at around Dated Brent -60 cents but was set to fall.
"Urals is steady at the moment but whether you'd find anybody to pay those numbers is a different matter," said a trader.
Iraq's aid distribution plan is expected to gain U.N. approval next week, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday, removing the last major obstacle to a resumption of exports.

Shipping brokers said U.S. trader Bayoil has provisionally fixed a ULCC from Ceyhan to take prompt loading Iraqi crude to the U.S., but other traders said they still did not expect anything to be shipped for another couple of weeks.
"They (Bayoil) have been fixing and failing vessels for a couple of weeks. We're still not expecting oil before (August) 15th," said one.
Traders said Greek and Moroccan tenders to buy one small cargo each of mid-August arrival Urals had been won by Glencore and BP respectively but that both requirements were already covered.
